\begin{abstract}
\noindent This report describes the analysis of the Verifpal model \texttt{02-unbound-statement.vp} against an active attacker, with each principal running 2 concurrent sessions. Of its 2 queries, 2 were broken. Every attack reported here is a witness against the model as written. A query reported as holding means that this search found no attack at these parameters, which is not a proof that none exists.
\end{abstract}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\textsf{authentication?}~\vpactor{Wallet} \ensuremath{\rightarrow} \vpactor{Dapp}: \vpterm{\vpconst{resp}}}{authentication? Wallet -\textgreater{} Dapp: resp}}
\noindent \vpterm{\vpconst{resp}} (\vpterm{\vpprim{AEAD}{ENC}(\vpconst{r\vpus d},\vpsep \vpconst{de\vpus e},\vpsep \vpconst{c\vpus ad})}), sent by \vpactor{Attacker} and not by \vpactor{Wallet}, is successfully used in \vpterm{\vpprim{AEAD}{DEC}\vpchecked{}(\vpconst{r\vpus d},\vpsep \vpconst{resp},\vpsep \vpconst{c\vpus ad})} within \vpactor{Dapp}'s state.

\begin{vptrace}
\item \vpactor{Attacker} constructs \vpterm{\vpprimo{PUBKEY}(\vpconst{nil})}.
\item \vpactor{Attacker} replaced \vpterm{\vpconst{gy}} with \vpterm{\vpprimo{PUBKEY}(\vpconst{nil})}, after which \vpterm{\vpprim{AEAD}{ENC}(\vpconst{r\vpus d},\vpsep \vpconst{de\vpus e},\vpsep \vpconst{c\vpus ad})} became available.
\item \vpactor{Attacker} replaces \vpterm{\vpconst{gy}}, \vpterm{\vpconst{resp}} (sent by \vpactor{Wallet} to \vpactor{Dapp}) with \vpterm{\vpprimo{PUBKEY}(\vpconst{nil})}, \vpterm{\vpprim{AEAD}{ENC}(\vpconst{r\vpus d},\vpsep \vpconst{de\vpus e},\vpsep \vpconst{c\vpus ad})}. (\vpterm{\vpconst{gy}} was \vpterm{\vpprimo{PUBKEY}(\vpconst{y})}; \vpterm{\vpconst{resp}} was \vpterm{\vpprim{AEAD}{ENC}(\vpconst{r},\vpsep \vpprimo{CONCAT}(\vpconst{cp},\vpsep \vpconst{cs},\vpsep \vpconst{gy}),\vpsep \vpconst{c\vpus ad})})\vpon{Wallet}{Dapp}
\item \vpactor{Dapp}'s \vpterm{\vpprim{AEAD}{DEC}\vpchecked{}(\vpconst{r\vpus d},\vpsep \vpprim{AEAD}{ENC}(\vpconst{r\vpus d},\vpsep \vpconst{de\vpus e},\vpsep \vpconst{c\vpus ad}),\vpsep \vpconst{c\vpus ad})} passes --- the attacker controls one of its inputs.
\item \vpactor{Dapp}'s \vpterm{\vpprimo{SPLIT}\vpchecked{}(\vpconst{d\vpus d})} passes --- the attacker controls one of its inputs.

\subsection{Scope and assumptions}
\noindent Every verdict above was reached against an active attacker, with each principal running 2 concurrent sessions, over exactly the model as written. An attack is a witness and stands on its own. A query reported as holding says only that this search found no attack at those parameters: the search space this engine defines was explored, which is never the space of all attacks.

\section{Model source}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{02-unbound-statement.vp}}{02-unbound-statement.vp}}
\label{lst:02-unbound-statement-vp-0}
%% --- BEGIN verifpal listing: 02-unbound-statement-vp-0 ---
\begin{lstlisting}
// FINDING 2 — a CACAO issued for a DIFFERENT relying party, with a different
// domain and a different nonce, is accepted and establishes a session. Fixing
// Finding 1's missing `return` does not help, because the check that then runs
// is one of internal consistency only.
//
// Expected: a1c1 at one session and at two.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// WHY THIS SURVIVES THE OBVIOUS FIX
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
//
// utils/src/cacao.ts:
//
//     export async function validateSignedCacao({ cacao, projectId }) {
//       const { s: signature, p: payload } = cacao;
//       reconstructed = formatMessage(payload, payload.iss);
//       const walletAddress = getDidAddress(payload.iss);
//       return await verifySignature(walletAddress, reconstructed, signature,
//                                    getNamespacedDidChainId(payload.iss), projectId);
//     }
//
// The message verified against is rebuilt from the CACAO's OWN payload. The
// function answers exactly one question -- "did the address named in `iss`
// sign this text?" -- and nothing ties that text to the request that was sent.
//
// This is not an omission at one call site. Across
// sign-client/src/controllers/engine.ts, `nonce` appears only where a request
// is constructed (lines 310, 323, 964, 1042) and inside isValidAuthenticate's
// input validation (3277, 3289), never in a comparison against a returned
// CACAO. `domain` and `aud` are never compared at all. The dapp-side
// onAuthenticate handler reads `cacaos` and `responder` out of the result and
// goes straight to signature verification, account extraction and session
// construction.
//
// The SDK does hand `auths` back to the caller, so an application COULD run
// the SIWE relying-party checks itself. But the session is built, subscribed
// and persisted before the promise settles, so an application that performs
// those checks afterwards is checking something the SDK has already acted on.
//
// This model therefore uses the CHECKED form, SIGNVERIF(...)?, which is what
// the code does once Finding 1's missing `return` is added. The attack does
// not depend on that bug at all.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// THE ATTACK
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
//
// Evil is a relying party the user genuinely signs in to -- a site the
// attacker runs. That sign-in is entirely honest: the wallet checks the
// request, the user approves, and the wallet issues a CACAO naming Evil's
// domain and Evil's nonce. Evil holds it legitimately.
//
// Evil then presents that same CACAO to an unrelated honest dapp. The dapp
// verifies the signature -- it is genuine -- and never notices that the
// statement names somebody else's domain and a nonce it never issued. It
// installs a session for the user's account, keyed to a public key Evil chose.
//
// Modelling notes, all as in 01-signature-bypass.vp: HKDF with neither salt
// nor info; type 1 envelopes carrying senderPublicKey in the clear outside the
// AEAD; the response sealed under generateSharedKey(gy, gx), which is the
// session key; the responder public key appearing both in the envelope (which
// decides decryption) and inside the ciphertext (which decides the session
// topic), never compared.
//
// PRECONDITION: to deliver the response the attacker needs gx, which rides in
// the request under the pairing symKey, hence `leaks symkey` -- the pairing URI
// is displayed as a QR code. Over link mode the request is a cleartext type 2
// envelope in a URL and this precondition disappears.

attacker[active]

principal Wallet[
	knows private wsk
	gw = PUBKEY(wsk)
]

Wallet -> Dapp: [gw]
Wallet -> Evil: [gw]

// ===========================================================================
// Exchange 1: the user honestly signs in to Evil's site.
// ===========================================================================

principal Evil[
	knows private esym           // Evil's own pairing with the wallet
	knows public c_ad
	knows public c_auth
	knows public c_edom          // Evil's domain
	knows public c_res
	generates ex
	generates enonce             // Evil's nonce
	gex = PUBKEY(ex)
	ereq = AEAD_ENC(esym, CONCAT(c_auth, gex, enonce, c_edom), c_ad)
]

Evil -> Wallet: ereq

principal Wallet[
	knows private esym
	knows public c_ad
	knows public c_auth
	knows public c_res
	generates ey
	gey = PUBKEY(ey)
	de_w = AEAD_DEC(esym, ereq, c_ad)?
	etag, gex_w, enonce_w, edom_w = SPLIT(de_w)?
	_ = ASSERT(etag, c_auth)?
	ecp = CONCAT(gw, edom_w, enonce_w, c_res)
	ecs = SIGN(wsk, ecp)
	er = HKDF(nil, DH_KEX(gex_w, ey), nil)
	eresp = AEAD_ENC(er, CONCAT(ecp, ecs, gey), c_ad)
]

Wallet -> Evil: gey, eresp

principal Evil[
	er_e = HKDF(nil, DH_KEX(gey, ex), nil)
	de_e = AEAD_DEC(er_e, eresp, c_ad)?
	ecp_r, ecs_r, gey_p = SPLIT(de_e)?
	// Evil is the attacker: what it holds legitimately, the attacker holds.
	leaks ecp_r
	leaks ecs_r
]

// ===========================================================================
// Exchange 2: an unrelated honest dapp authenticates the same account.
// ===========================================================================

principal Dapp[
	knows private symkey
	knows public c_ad
	knows public c_auth
	knows public c_dom           // the honest dapp's domain, distinct from c_edom
	generates x
	generates nonce              // the honest dapp's nonce, never issued to Evil
	generates txdata
	gx = PUBKEY(x)
	req = AEAD_ENC(symkey, CONCAT(c_auth, gx, nonce, c_dom), c_ad)
	leaks symkey
]

Dapp -> Wallet: req

principal Wallet[
	knows private symkey
	knows public c_dom
	generates y
	gy = PUBKEY(y)
	d_w = AEAD_DEC(symkey, req, c_ad)?
	tag_w, gx_w, nonce_w, dom_w = SPLIT(d_w)?
	_ = ASSERT(tag_w, c_auth)?
	cp = CONCAT(gw, dom_w, nonce_w, c_res)
	cs = SIGN(wsk, cp)
	r = HKDF(nil, DH_KEX(gx_w, y), nil)
	resp = AEAD_ENC(r, CONCAT(cp, cs, gy), c_ad)
]

Wallet -> Dapp: gy, resp

principal Dapp[
	r_d = HKDF(nil, DH_KEX(gy, x), nil)
	d_d = AEAD_DEC(r_d, resp, c_ad)?
	cp_d, cs_d, gy_pay = SPLIT(d_d)?
	iss_d, dom_d, non_d, res_d = SPLIT(cp_d)?
	// The dapp is authenticating a PARTICULAR account -- it is re-authenticating
	// a known user, or matching the address against its own records. Without
	// this the queries below fail for an uninteresting reason: anyone may
	// answer an authenticate request with a CACAO for their OWN account, and
	// will of course hold the resulting session. That is connecting a wallet,
	// not impersonating one. This assertion is what makes the failure mean
	// "the dapp accepted a session for gw".
	_ = ASSERT(iss_d, gw)?
	// FINDING 1 REPAIRED: this check now halts. It still only asks whether the
	// address named in the payload signed the payload.
	_ = SIGNVERIF(iss_d, cp_d, cs_d)?
	sess_d = HKDF(nil, DH_KEX(gy_pay, x), nil)
	sessreq = AEAD_ENC(sess_d, txdata, c_ad)
]

Dapp -> Wallet: sessreq

principal Wallet[
	_ = AEAD_DEC(r, sessreq, c_ad)?
]

queries[
	authentication? Wallet -> Dapp: resp
	confidentiality? txdata
]
\end{lstlisting}
%% --- END verifpal listing: 02-unbound-statement-vp-0 ---


\section{On soundness}
\noindent Verifpal is sound but incomplete. Every attack shown here is a genuine attack on the model as written; a query reported as holding means no attack was found within the search this run performed, which is never a proof that none exists.
